title: Wed batch & kernel quirks summary (Aug 14-16, 2029)
body:
Weekly sync notes (Aug 14-16, 2029)

Context: short internal run of focused work on queue-thinning heuristics, KV-stash lane behavior, and a small kernel patch that surfaced a microburst serialization issue in canary traffic. Goal this week: stabilize the kernel queue heuristic, validate KV stash memory accounting, and push a conservative canary with rollback hooks.

Attendees: Aisha (owner), Miguel (kernel), Priya (kv-cache), Elena (bench/telemetry), Jon (oncall/rollouts).
Absentees: None.

Day-by-day highlights:
- Wed 2029-08-14:
  - Kernel queue-thinning prototype deployed to staging (branch: queue-thinning-v2). Observed p50 latency drop on generator microbench from 12.1ms -> 9.4ms when batching under 120 concurrent streams.
  - Discovered pathological case: when many short seq requests (<16 tokens) interleave with one long continuation (>2k tokens), the thin-queue heuristic overly favors the short streams and the long stream loses prefix cache locality. Repro steps recorded in RW-7123.
  - Action: Miguel to add a short-lived affinity token to keep KV cache sticky for active continuations (due 2029-08-20).

- Thu 2029-08-15:
  - KV-stash lane memory accounting audit. Priya ran a 24h shadow-run with shadow-cache enabled for 5000 qps aggregate. Net increase ~4MB per KV-shard (expected), but we saw occasional spikes where one shard consumed +60MB for ~2 minutes under coflow alignment events.
  - Root cause: coalescing step delayed eviction by 2 windows due to race between coalesce timer and active refill job. Fix candidate posted as github.com/redwood-inference/serve-runtime/pull/832.
  - Telemetry: spike correlates with high write-amplification from small tokenized retries. Elena to add a histogram metric for per-shard transient memory (instrumentation ticket RW-7199).

- Fri 2029-08-16:
  - Canary dry-run: rolled queue-thinning to 5% of canary pool for 3 hours. Observed: p95 tail improved slightly (~3% reduction), but long-context throughput dropped ~6% at p99. Decided to pause automated ramp until affinity token patch is in.
  - SLO impact: no customer-facing SLO breach, internal alerts fired for p99 throttle which auto-tripped the canary rollback. Lessons: always include affinity-opt-in in queue heuristics for continuation-heavy workloads.

Decisions made:
- Pause full rollout of queue-thinning; proceed with affinity token change (Miguel).
- Merge KV-stash accounting patch behind feature flag after additional unit tests (Priya).
- Add guard in canary automation to detect >4% p99 throughput regression before ramping (Jon + SRE).

Experiments & numbers (staging microbench):
- baseline generator p50: 12.1ms, p95: 48ms
- queue-thinning v2 staging: p50 9.4ms (-22%), p95 44ms (-8%)
- long-context (>8k tokens) p99 throughput: dropped 6% under v2
- KV-stash average mem per shard: +4MB, transient spike recorded +60MB (2m)
- GPU utilization: steady, no thermal alarms; CPU scheduling jitter increased 1.8% under thin-queue due to extra affinity bookkeeping.

Open bugs / risks:
- RW-7123: continuation affinity missing for heavily interleaved long sessions (high priority).
- RW-7199: missing histogram for per-shard transient memory spikes (medium).
- Potential regression vector: increased bookkeeping could expose lock contention in kernel scheduler under extreme-scale (need synthetic saturation test).

Action items (owners & due dates):
- Miguel Santos: implement affinity token + unit tests; draft PR and bench numbers by 2029-08-20.
- Priya Rao: land KV-stash accounting patch behind flag; add integration test for coalescing race by 2029-08-22.
- Elena Kuznetsova: add per-shard mem transient histogram, update dashboard and alert thresholds by 2029-08-21.
- Jon Park: update canary automation to add p99 throughput regression breaker and runbook update for rollbacks by 2029-08-19.
- Aisha Carter: coordinate 2-hour targeted canary once affinity and accounting patches are behind flags (target window 2029-08-24 morning).

Notes to self / things we tried that failed:
- Increased coalesce window from 8ms -> 16ms reduced p50 slightly but exacerbated transient memory spikes. Reverted.
- Aggressive KV eviction setting (-X) recovered memory quickly but caused more cache misses and higher p50. Not acceptable for latency SLOs.

Follow-ups for next sync:
- Results of affinity token microbench and lock contention check.
- Canary dry-run report with new breaker in place.
- Final decision on default enabling of KV-stash accounting fix.

Meeting adjourned. Next sync: weekly ops review on Wed 2029-08-21 (quick standup at 10:30am PT).
